title: Multimodal Electron Microscopy Characterization of Electrochemically Formed δ Phase in Manganese-Rich Rocksalt Cathodes
content: Lithium-ion (Li-ion) batteries are critical to technological advancement due to their high energy density and extended lifespan. However, traditional cathode materials, which mainly utilize layered and spinel structures, rely on scarce and controversial resources such as nickel (Ni) and cobalt (Co) [1,2]. In this regard, manganese (Mn)-based cathodes are emerging as high-capacity, abundant alternatives, offering optimal voltage and stability. Significantly, the improved performance of disordered rocksalt (DRX) materials with high Mn content is associated with their transformation into a novel δ-phase [3]. This phase is distinguished by its partially disordered nature at various scales, making it challenging for conventional characterization methods. In our study, we utilize scanning electron nano diffraction (SEND) with a pixelated detector, combined with high-resolution high angle annular dark field (HAADF)-STEM imaging, to investigate the atomic structure and transformational behavior of the δ-phase [4,5]. The insights derived from these analyses are essential for exploring new synthesis methods of δ-phase cathodes from DRX precursors.
